title: Top show per country
context: Every market has its own #1.
task: Return country, title and minutes for the most-watched show (by SUM(minutes_watched)) in each user country; ties by title ascending.
hint: Aggregate country+show, then ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY country.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT u.country, s.title, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN users u ON u.user_id = w.user_id JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY u.country, s.show_id) SELECT country, title, minutes FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY minutes DESC, title) AS rn FROM t) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Each user's first watch
context: What title hooks new users?
task: Return user_id, title and watch_date of each user's earliest session (ties by lowest view_id).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_date, view_id).
answer: SELECT user_id, title, watch_date FROM (SELECT w.user_id, s.title, w.watch_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY w.user_id ORDER BY w.watch_date, w.view_id) AS rn FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Top 2 genres per country
context: Regional genre preferences.
task: Return country, genre and minutes for the top 2 genres by minutes in each user country (DENSE_RANK; ties included).
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY minutes DESC) <= 2.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT u.country, s.genre, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN users u ON u.user_id = w.user_id JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY u.country, s.genre) SELECT country, genre, minutes FROM (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY minutes DESC) AS rk FROM t) WHERE rk <= 2;

title: Cumulative minutes by month
context: The 'total hours streamed' counter grows month by month.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM), minutes and cumulative_minutes (running sum ordered by month).
hint: SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY month).
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', watch_date) AS month, SUM(minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY month) SELECT month, minutes, SUM(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS cumulative_minutes FROM m;

title: Month-over-month change in active viewers
context: Growth or decline in distinct viewers per month.
task: Return month, viewers = distinct users with a session that month, and change = viewers minus previous month's viewers (NULL first), ordered by month.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) then LAG.
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', watch_date) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS viewers FROM watch_history GROUP BY month) SELECT month, viewers, viewers - LAG(viewers) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change FROM m;

title: Gap between a user's sessions
context: Long gaps predict churn.
task: Return user_id, view_id and gap_days = days since that user's previous session (integer), only where a previous session exists.
hint: LAG(watch_date) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_date, view_id).
answer: SELECT user_id, view_id, gap_days FROM (SELECT user_id, view_id, CAST(julianday(watch_date) - julianday(LAG(watch_date) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_date, view_id)) AS INTEGER) AS gap_days FROM watch_history) WHERE gap_days IS NOT NULL;

title: Engagement quartiles
context: Segment users into four tiers by total minutes.
task: Return user_id, total_minutes and quartile = NTILE(4) ordered by total_minutes descending (1 = most engaged).
hint: Aggregate in a CTE first.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT user_id, SUM(minutes_watched) AS total_minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id) SELECT user_id, total_minutes, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_minutes DESC) AS quartile FROM t;

title: Each show's share of its genre
context: Within Thriller, how dominant is the top title?
task: Return genre, title and pct_of_genre = show minutes / genre minutes * 100 (1 decimal) for every show with sessions.
hint: SUM(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY genre).
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT s.genre, s.title, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY s.show_id) SELECT genre, title, ROUND(minutes * 100.0 / SUM(minutes) OVER (PARTITION BY genre), 1) AS pct_of_genre FROM t;

title: 7-day rolling minutes
context: Smooth daily engagement.
task: Return watch_date, minutes (that day's total) and rolling7 = average of the daily total over the current and 6 preceding rows (2 decimals), ordered by date.
hint: ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT watch_date, SUM(minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY watch_date) SELECT watch_date, minutes, ROUND(AVG(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY watch_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS rolling7 FROM d;

title: Binge days
context: A binge = 3 or more sessions of the same series on one day.
task: Return user_id, title, watch_date and episodes = session count, for (user, show, date) groups with 3+ sessions where the show's type is 'Series'.
hint: GROUP BY user, show, date HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
answer: SELECT w.user_id, s.title, w.watch_date, COUNT(*) AS episodes FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id WHERE s.type = 'Series' GROUP BY w.user_id, w.show_id, w.watch_date HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

title: Bingers vs non-bingers: average rating
context: Do people who binge rate content higher?
task: Return group_name ('binger' for users with at least one binge day as defined above, else 'other') and avg_rating (2 decimals) from ratings.
hint: CTE of binger user_ids; CASE in GROUP BY.
answer: WITH b AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id, show_id, watch_date HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) SELECT CASE WHEN r.user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM b) THEN 'binger' ELSE 'other' END AS group_name, ROUND(AVG(r.rating), 2) AS avg_rating FROM ratings r GROUP BY group_name;

title: Signup cohort retention at 30 days
context: Of users who signed up each year, what share watched something within 30 days?
task: Return signup_year and active_30_pct = users with a session within 30 days of signup / users in that year * 100 (1 decimal).
hint: EXISTS with a julianday window inside a conditional SUM.
answer: SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', u.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS signup_year, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM watch_history w WHERE w.user_id = u.user_id AND julianday(w.watch_date) - julianday(u.signup_date) <= 30) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS active_30_pct FROM users u GROUP BY signup_year;

title: Users active in consecutive months
context: Monthly retention: watched in month m and month m-1.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and retained = users with a session in that month and in the previous calendar month, ordered by month; only months with retained > 0.
hint: Distinct (user, month) pairs self-joined on previous month.
answer: WITH um AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, strftime('%Y-%m', watch_date) AS month FROM watch_history) SELECT a.month, COUNT(*) AS retained FROM um a JOIN um b ON b.user_id = a.user_id AND b.month = strftime('%Y-%m', date(a.month || '-01', '-1 month')) GROUP BY a.month ORDER BY a.month;

title: Silent subscribers
context: Active subscription but no session in the last 90 days (as of 2025-07-31) — churn risk.
task: Return user_id and last_watch for users with an 'active' subscription whose latest watch_date is more than 90 days before '2025-07-31'.
hint: Join subscriptions; HAVING on julianday difference.
answer: SELECT w.user_id, MAX(w.watch_date) AS last_watch FROM watch_history w JOIN subscriptions s ON s.user_id = w.user_id AND s.status = 'active' GROUP BY w.user_id HAVING julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(w.watch_date)) > 90;

title: Minutes in the last 30 days before cancelling
context: Did cancelled users go quiet first?
task: For each cancelled subscription return subscription_id, user_id and final_30_minutes = minutes watched in the 30 days up to and including end_date (0 if none).
hint: LEFT JOIN watch_history with a date window in ON.
answer: SELECT s.subscription_id, s.user_id, COALESCE(SUM(w.minutes_watched), 0) AS final_30_minutes FROM subscriptions s LEFT JOIN watch_history w ON w.user_id = s.user_id AND w.watch_date <= s.end_date AND julianday(s.end_date) - julianday(w.watch_date) <= 30 WHERE s.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY s.subscription_id;

title: Upgrade path
context: Which plan did users move to after an upgrade?
task: Return from_plan, to_plan and users = number of users who had a subscription with status 'upgraded' followed by their next subscription (by start_date).
hint: Self-join subscriptions on user where next.start_date = prev.end_date, or use LEAD.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT user_id, plan, status, LEAD(plan) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY start_date) AS next_plan FROM subscriptions) SELECT plan AS from_plan, next_plan AS to_plan, COUNT(*) AS users FROM s WHERE status = 'upgraded' AND next_plan IS NOT NULL GROUP BY plan, next_plan;

title: Current plan derived from history
context: Ignore users.plan — derive it from the latest subscription row.
task: Return user_id and current_plan = plan of the subscription with the latest start_date per user.
hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY start_date DESC) = 1.
answer: SELECT user_id, plan AS current_plan FROM (SELECT user_id, plan, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY start_date DESC, subscription_id DESC) AS rn FROM subscriptions) WHERE rn = 1;

title: users.plan out of sync
context: Check the denormalised users.plan against the latest subscription.
task: Return user_id, users.plan AS listed_plan and latest_plan where they differ.
hint: Use the previous query as a CTE and compare.
answer: WITH cur AS (SELECT user_id, plan FROM (SELECT user_id, plan, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY start_date DESC, subscription_id DESC) AS rn FROM subscriptions) WHERE rn = 1) SELECT u.user_id, u.plan AS listed_plan, cur.plan AS latest_plan FROM users u JOIN cur ON cur.user_id = u.user_id WHERE u.plan <> cur.plan;

title: MRR by month, from subscription intervals
context: For each month, sum monthly_price of subscriptions active on the 1st of that month.
task: Using a recursive CTE for months 2023-01 to 2025-07, return month (YYYY-MM) and mrr (2 decimals) = sum of monthly_price where start_date <= first of month AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > first of month).
hint: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) ... LEFT JOIN subscriptions on the interval.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) AS (SELECT '2023-01-01' UNION ALL SELECT date(m, '+1 month') FROM months WHERE m < '2025-07-01') SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', m) AS month, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(s.monthly_price), 0), 2) AS mrr FROM months LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON s.start_date <= m AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > m) GROUP BY m ORDER BY m;

title: Revenue per minute watched
context: How much revenue does each minute of content cost us to earn, per plan?
task: Return plan, revenue (sum of monthly_price × months as in the lifetime-revenue question, 2 decimals) and minutes, and revenue_per_minute (4 decimals) grouped by subscription plan; attribute a user's minutes to their latest plan.
hint: Two CTEs: revenue per plan, minutes per user's latest plan; join on plan.
answer: WITH cur AS (SELECT user_id, plan FROM (SELECT user_id, plan, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY start_date DESC, subscription_id DESC) AS rn FROM subscriptions) WHERE rn = 1), rev AS (SELECT plan, SUM(monthly_price * (julianday(COALESCE(end_date, '2025-07-31')) - julianday(start_date)) / 30.0) AS revenue FROM subscriptions GROUP BY plan), mins AS (SELECT cur.plan, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN cur ON cur.user_id = w.user_id GROUP BY cur.plan) SELECT rev.plan, ROUND(rev.revenue, 2) AS revenue, mins.minutes, ROUND(rev.revenue / mins.minutes, 4) AS revenue_per_minute FROM rev JOIN mins ON mins.plan = rev.plan;

title: Longest daily viewing streak per user
context: Consecutive days with at least one session.
task: Return user_id and longest_streak = the maximum run of consecutive watch dates for that user.
hint: Distinct dates per user; date(d, -ROW_NUMBER days) is constant within a streak.
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, watch_date FROM watch_history), g AS (SELECT user_id, watch_date, date(watch_date, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY watch_date) || ' days') AS grp FROM d), s AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS streak FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp) SELECT user_id, MAX(streak) AS longest_streak FROM s GROUP BY user_id;

title: Also watched by
context: 'Because you watched Dark': titles most co-watched with show 8 by the same users.
task: Return title and shared_viewers = number of distinct users who watched both show 8 and this show, excluding show 8 itself, ordered by shared_viewers desc then title, top 5.
hint: Self-join watch_history on user_id.
answer: SELECT s.title, COUNT(DISTINCT a.user_id) AS shared_viewers FROM watch_history a JOIN watch_history b ON b.user_id = a.user_id AND b.show_id <> 8 JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = b.show_id WHERE a.show_id = 8 GROUP BY b.show_id ORDER BY shared_viewers DESC, s.title LIMIT 5;

title: Genre affinity score
context: For each user, the genre with the highest share of their minutes.
task: Return user_id, genre and pct = that genre's share of the user's minutes (1 decimal), one row per user (ties by genre ascending).
hint: Share via SUM OVER (PARTITION BY user_id), then ROW_NUMBER.
answer: WITH g AS (SELECT w.user_id, s.genre, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS m FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY w.user_id, s.genre), p AS (SELECT user_id, genre, m * 100.0 / SUM(m) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id) AS pct FROM g) SELECT user_id, genre, ROUND(pct, 1) AS pct FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY pct DESC, genre) AS rn FROM p) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Catalogue freshness
context: What share of minutes goes to content released in the last 3 years (2022+)?
task: Return fresh_pct = minutes on shows with release_year >= 2022 / all minutes * 100 (1 decimal).
hint: Conditional SUM / SUM.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.release_year >= 2022 THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / SUM(w.minutes_watched), 1) AS fresh_pct FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id;

title: Under-performing originals
context: Shows whose minutes are below the median show minutes AND whose average rating is below 3.
task: Return title, minutes and avg_rating (2 decimals) for shows below the median of per-show minutes and with average rating < 3 (must have at least one rating).
hint: Median via ROW_NUMBER/COUNT; join ratings aggregate.
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT show_id, SUM(minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY show_id), med AS (SELECT AVG(minutes) AS median FROM (SELECT minutes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY minutes) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt FROM m) WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)), r AS (SELECT show_id, AVG(rating) AS avg_rating FROM ratings GROUP BY show_id) SELECT s.title, m.minutes, ROUND(r.avg_rating, 2) AS avg_rating FROM m JOIN r ON r.show_id = m.show_id JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = m.show_id WHERE m.minutes < (SELECT median FROM med) AND r.avg_rating < 3;

title: Top 10% sessions by length
context: Marathon sessions.
task: Return view_id and minutes_watched for sessions with PERCENT_RANK (ordered by minutes_watched) >= 0.9.
hint: PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY minutes_watched).
answer: SELECT view_id, minutes_watched FROM (SELECT view_id, minutes_watched, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY minutes_watched) AS pr FROM watch_history) WHERE pr >= 0.9;

title: Minutes by genre × device
context: Wide report: TV, Mobile, Laptop, Tablet columns per genre.
task: Return genre, tv, mobile, laptop, tablet = minutes on each device.
hint: One SUM(CASE ...) per column.
answer: SELECT s.genre, SUM(CASE WHEN w.device = 'TV' THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS tv, SUM(CASE WHEN w.device = 'Mobile' THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS mobile, SUM(CASE WHEN w.device = 'Laptop' THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS laptop, SUM(CASE WHEN w.device = 'Tablet' THEN w.minutes_watched ELSE 0 END) AS tablet FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY s.genre;

title: Users who watched every Documentary
context: Completionists of a genre.
task: Return user_id for users who have watched every show in the 'Documentary' genre at least once.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT show_id) filtered to the genre = total documentaries.
answer: SELECT w.user_id FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id WHERE s.genre = 'Documentary' GROUP BY w.user_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT w.show_id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shows WHERE genre = 'Documentary');

title: Did the first show they watched keep them?
context: Compare each user's first-watched genre with their most-watched genre.
task: Return user_id, first_genre and top_genre (by minutes; ties by genre), only for users where the two differ.
hint: FIRST_VALUE for the first; the affinity CTE for the top.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT DISTINCT w.user_id, FIRST_VALUE(s.genre) OVER (PARTITION BY w.user_id ORDER BY w.watch_date, w.view_id) AS first_genre FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id), g AS (SELECT w.user_id, s.genre, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS m FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY w.user_id, s.genre), t AS (SELECT user_id, genre AS top_genre FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY m DESC, genre) AS rn FROM g) WHERE rn = 1) SELECT f.user_id, f.first_genre, t.top_genre FROM f JOIN t ON t.user_id = f.user_id WHERE f.first_genre <> t.top_genre;

title: Average sessions per active week
context: Frequency, not volume: sessions ÷ distinct weeks with any session.
task: Return user_id and sessions_per_week = COUNT(*) / COUNT(DISTINCT week) as a 2-decimal number, where week = strftime('%Y-%W', watch_date).
hint: COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%W', watch_date)).
answer: SELECT user_id, ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%W', watch_date)), 2) AS sessions_per_week FROM watch_history GROUP BY user_id;

title: Second most-watched show per genre
context: The runner-up in every genre.
task: Return genre, title and minutes for the show ranked 2nd by minutes within its genre (DENSE_RANK = 2).
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY genre ORDER BY minutes DESC).
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT s.genre, s.title, SUM(w.minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history w JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = w.show_id GROUP BY s.show_id) SELECT genre, title, minutes FROM (SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY genre ORDER BY minutes DESC) AS rk FROM t) WHERE rk = 2;

title: Ratings and minutes without fan-out
context: A naive join of watch_history and ratings multiplies rows. Get both numbers correctly.
task: Return title, minutes = total minutes watched, and ratings_count, for every show with sessions; ratings_count is 0 when unrated.
hint: Aggregate the two tables separately, then LEFT JOIN.
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT show_id, SUM(minutes_watched) AS minutes FROM watch_history GROUP BY show_id), r AS (SELECT show_id, COUNT(*) AS ratings_count FROM ratings GROUP BY show_id) SELECT s.title, m.minutes, COALESCE(r.ratings_count, 0) AS ratings_count FROM m JOIN shows s ON s.show_id = m.show_id LEFT JOIN r ON r.show_id = m.show_id;

title: Every month a user was subscribed
context: Expand user 1's subscription intervals into one row per month.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) for every calendar month between user 1's earliest start_date and '2025-07-31' during which they had a subscription active on the 1st, ordered by month.
hint: Recursive month series from MIN(start_date), then EXISTS on the interval.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) AS (SELECT date((SELECT MIN(start_date) FROM subscriptions WHERE user_id = 1), 'start of month') UNION ALL SELECT date(m, '+1 month') FROM months WHERE m < '2025-07-01') SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', m) AS month FROM months WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions s WHERE s.user_id = 1 AND s.start_date <= m AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > m)) ORDER BY m;
